text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- B.C. Coho just aren't there, survey: Canada can't haggle with United States over catch quotas because there are too few fish.
- Act on pollution, APEC urged: Group's credibility called on the line.
- Slashing is over, Liberals predict: Party to put on a beneficient face.
- Bird study sings a different tune: Migratory populations actually stable.
- Budget crisis grips German government: Kohl urged to step down as coalition backing his government near collapse.
- Knowles will be honored in special fashion, PM says: Legendary New Democrat praised by Ottawa colleagues.
- Parmalat makes bid for Ault: C$415-million offer by Italian company tops hostile bid by Montreal's Saputo Group.
- Eaton's chief pegs need at up to C$300 million: Kosich says family, share issue among possible capital sources.
- Fund manager wants more for Southam shares: Black's bid should be at least C$25 share, U.S.-based Franklin Mutual says.
- N.Y. developer eyes Toronto site: Millennium has designs on land adjacent to Eaton Centre.
- U.S. company bids to take over Domco: Follows earlier offer from Tarkett.
- Parmalat ups Ault stakes: Italian dairy giant rides to the rescue with C$415-million friendly offer that tops a hostile bid by Saputo Group and would see Ault merged with Beatrice.
- U.S. investor balks at Black's Southam offer.
